pattern: Leaderless partitioned replication: place keys on a hash ring with virtual nodes, keep N copies, let callers trade consistency for availability with R/W quorums, version values so concurrent writes are detected rather than lost, and heal in the background (hinted handoff, read repair, Merkle-tree anti-entropy) with gossip for membership.

tips.nudge: What can a caller do with this store?
tips.hint: List the operations and their arguments.
tips.show: F1: put(key, value), get(key), delete(key); keys ≤ 256 B, values ≤ 1 MB.

tips.nudge: The cart team said something strong about writes.
tips.hint: State what must keep working when servers or a zone are unreachable.
tips.show: N1: Highly available: writes are accepted during node failures and network partitions (AP by default).

tips.nudge: After a write, what may a read return? Do all callers need the same answer?
tips.hint: Name the default consistency model and the stronger option.
tips.show: N2: Eventually consistent by default with conflicts surfaced to the client; tunable per request (quorum reads for stronger guarantees).

tips.nudge: The interviewer gave a number for both reads and writes.
tips.hint: State a latency target and the load it must hold at.
tips.show: N3: p99 < 10 ms for get and put at 1M reads/s + 200k writes/s.

tips.nudge: Keys × bytes per entry, and don't forget the copies.
tips.hint: raw = 20B × (~1 KB value + key + metadata); then × replication factor.

tips.nudge: Each server has 4 TB, and ops wants it half empty.
tips.hint: nodes = replicated bytes / (4 TB × 0.5); check throughput per node too.
tips.show: 72 TB / 2 TB per node ≈ 36 nodes (round up to ~40 for headroom).

tips.nudge: Replication multiplies requests. How many land on each server?
tips.show: (1M × 2 + 200k × 3) / 36 ≈ 72k replica operations/s per node: fine for SSD + memtable.

tips.nudge: What does a caller send to store a value, and what comes back?
tips.hint: Think about what the caller must pass back so the store can tell an update from a conflict.
tips.show: PUT /kv/{key} {value, context (version vector from the last get), w?} → 200 {context}

tips.nudge: Can a read return more than one value?
tips.hint: A GET by key that may return several concurrent versions plus a context.
tips.show: GET /kv/{key}?r=2 → 200 {values[], context} (several values = siblings to merge) or 404

tips.nudge: Key and value are not enough when two replicas disagree.
tips.hint: Store what you need to order or detect concurrent writes, and to delete safely.
tips.show: record(key, value, version vector [(node, counter)…], tombstone flag, ts) in an LSM tree (memtable + SSTables) per node.

checks.label: Something sends each request to the right servers

tips.nudge: A client has a key. Which of 40 servers should it talk to?
tips.hint: Some component (a node or a smart client) knows the ring and forwards to the owners.
tips.show: Request coordinator: any node (or a ring-aware client library) hashes the key and talks to the N replicas.

tips.nudge: How does every node learn that a node joined, left or died?
tips.hint: Some way to agree on who is in the cluster and who owns which ranges.
tips.show: Gossip-based membership + failure detector; each node holds the ring map (seed nodes bootstrap it).

checks.label: Requests reach the servers that own the key

tips.nudge: Draw the path from the router to the data.
tips.hint: Connect the coordinator to the storage nodes that hold replicas.
tips.show: Coordinator → storage nodes A, B, C (the key's preference list).

checks.label: How keys map to servers decided

tips.nudge: With hash(key) mod N, what happens to most keys when N goes from 40 to 41?
tips.hint: Compare modulo hashing, range partitioning and consistent hashing.
tips.show: Consistent hashing with ~256 virtual nodes per server: adding a server moves ~1/N of keys, spread evenly; heterogeneous servers get more vnodes.

checks.label: How many copies must answer decided

tips.nudge: 3 copies. A write waits for how many? A read asks how many?
tips.hint: Relate N, R and W; what does R + W > N buy you?
tips.show: N=3 across AZs, W=2, R=2 by default (R+W>N: reads overlap the latest write); callers may pick W=1 (fast, AP) or R=3. Sloppy quorum keeps writes available in a partition.

checks.label: Concurrent writes to one key resolved

tips.nudge: Both sides of a split accepted a write to the same cart. What does the next read see?
tips.hint: Compare last-write-wins timestamps with version vectors (and CRDTs).
tips.show: Version vectors detect concurrent writes; both versions are returned as siblings and the client merges (cart union); LWW is offered for data where losing one write is acceptable.

checks.label: Detecting and healing failed or stale replicas

tips.nudge: A node was down 2 hours. How does it get the writes it missed?
tips.hint: Name mechanisms for short outages, for reads that see disagreement, and for slow drift.
tips.show: Gossip failure detection; hinted handoff (a neighbour keeps writes for the dead node and replays them); read repair on mismatched reads; periodic Merkle-tree comparison per range (anti-entropy).

tips.nudge: Walk through: one node dies; one AZ is cut off; a disk silently corrupts data.
tips.hint: For each, say what callers see and how the system heals.
tips.show: Node down: sloppy quorum + hints, no caller impact. AZ cut off: replicas in other AZs serve quorum ops. Corruption: checksums per block, Merkle repair from peers. Permanent loss: re-replicate its ranges.

tips.nudge: Capacity grows 50% a year. What does adding 20 servers look like?
tips.hint: How data moves, how fast, and without downtime.
tips.show: New nodes take vnodes from many peers in parallel; streaming is throttled; the ring update gossips out; no downtime. Hot keys: client-side caching or key splitting.
